theme.name: Scope and definition of the ban
theme.claim: The ban will apply to solid microplastic ingredients under 5mm used in rinse-off cosmetics and personal care products such as exfoliating scrubs, shower gels and toothpastes, across the whole UK including devolved administrations.

text.line: The proposals would extend and apply to the UK including Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
the ban would apply to solid microplastic ingredients <5mm in size in every
dimension that are used as an ingredients in rinse-off cosmetics and personal care products including but not limited to exfoliating scrubs, shower gels and toothpastes.
This proposed ban applies to rinse-off cosmetics and personal care products
including but not limited to exfoliating scrubs, shower gels and toothpastes.

theme.name: Phased timetable for manufacture and sale
theme.claim: The ban will be phased in with manufacture prohibited from January 2018 and sale from June 2018 in England, with the legislation in force by October 2017, to allow businesses, especially SMEs, time to comply.

text.line: c. in England, the legislation is expected to come into force by 1st October 2017,
the latest common commencement date in 2017 for regulation bearing on business.
d. in England, the ban on manufacture is expected to apply from 1 January 2018
and the ban on sale expected from 30 June 2018.
The phased introduction of the ban is designed to provide sufficient time for small- and medium-sized enterprises to comply with requirements as outlined.

theme.name: Devolved and collaborative legislative approach
theme.claim: The legislation will be developed collaboratively with the Devolved Administrations, each introducing their own secondary legislation according to their own timetables while coordinating with England's approach.

text.line: We will aim to coordinate our approach with Devolved Administrations who will introduce legislation according to their own legislative processes and timetables.
We will aim to coordinate our approach with Devolved Administrations who will introduce legislation according to their own legislative processes and timetables.
e. the legislation will be developed collaboratively with the Devolved
Administrations and secondary legislation introduced to implement the proposed ban across the whole of the UK.
It is expected that such legislation
will be made by each Administration as a result of the devolution settlements.
It is expected that the implementing legislation will be published prior to it being made and therefore those with an interest will be able to make representations on it.

theme.name: Enforcement through civil sanctions
theme.claim: In England the ban is proposed to be enforced through civil sanctions under the Regulatory Enforcement and Sanctions Act 2008, requiring creation of an offence punishable by fine, with views sought on effective enforcement.

text.line: f. in England, it is proposed that the policy will in practice be enforced through

civil sanctions set out in part 3 of the Regulatory Enforcement and Sanctions Act 2008 (though this would require the creation of an offence punishable by a fine, to facilitate the use of the 2008 Act).
As part of the consultation, we are seeking views on how such civil enforcement can most effectively and proportionately be carried out.
The Devolved Administrations will establish appropriate enforcement mechanisms and would welcome views on this issue.

Details of the types of civil sanctions available are set out in the Regulatory Enforcement and Sanctions Act 2008 Part 3 Civil Sanctions sections in particular sections 39, 42 and 46. ** (Reference: 12)
They do not apply to overseas territories.
Our proposals for enforcement are set out at point (f) on page 9.
